text:
The Penguins arrived in Buffalo with five straight losses and a week of trade talk swirling around Erik Karlsson and Rickard Rakell. They left with a 6-3 win built largely by players who weren't part of the old core: Ben Kindel, Rutger McGroarty and Ville Koivunen each scored once and set up another.

Buffalo started like it meant to bury them. Jiri Kulich scored 31 seconds in, and after Kindel batted one out of the air to tie it, Rasmus Dahlin restored the lead on a power play at 9:19. The Sabres had 1.07 expected goals (the quality of their chances, added up) in the first to Pittsburgh's 0.29. Then Kris Letang scored on a 4% wrist shot with 40 seconds left in the period, the least likely goal of the night, and everything tilted.

McGroarty's deflection 30 seconds into the second gave Pittsburgh its first lead, and Blake Lizotte made it 4-2 at 3:15, with Karlsson picking up an assist. That was it for Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen: four goals on 10 shots, about 3.4 more than those shots deserved. Josh Norris pulled Buffalo within one on a 74% chance, but Koivunen answered at 18:44 on a shot that went through Alex Lyon after a Sabres turnover. Joe Yerdon of Bleacher Report called the period "A brutal second period for the Sabres like the ones we've seen before." Evgeni Malkin, whose name keeps showing up in Wild trade rumors, closed it at 17:59 of the third.

Here is the uncomfortable part for Pittsburgh: Buffalo won the chances 3.04 to 2.25 and won our replays of every shot 75% of the time. Sergei Murashov was solid, 20 saves on 23 shots and right at what those shots deserved, but the Penguins mostly scored on looks that usually don't go in. They will take it. For the Sabres, a team that had been getting hot nights from Tage Thompson and Jack Quinn, this one turned on goaltending, and that is the kind of loss that is hardest to fix with effort alone.
headline: Penguins' kids end the skid as Luukkonen's night ends early
